faqs.question: When is Vinayagar Chaturthi in 2026, and what is the puja time in Chennai?
faqs.answer: Monday 14 September 2026. Drik Panchang's Chennai listing gives a Madhyahna Ganesha Puja Muhurat of 10:51 AM to 1:18 PM, a window of 2 hours 27 minutes, with the Chaturthi tithi running from 07:06 AM on 14 September to 07:44 AM on 15 September.

faqs.question: Should the wish mention ten days, or is Vinayagar Chaturthi one day in Tamil Nadu?
faqs.answer: Put 14 September on the wish and leave the length out of it. Drik Panchang lists Chennai's Ganesha Visarjan on Anant Chaturdashi, Friday 25 September 2026, but how many days a household actually keeps the idol varies, so a wish that assumes ten days can be wrong for the person reading it.

faqs.question: What is the Pillaiyar suzhi, and does it belong in a written wish?
faqs.answer: The Tamil Lexicon defines பிள்ளையார்சுழி as the 'உ' mark drawn for auspiciousness when you begin to write. It belongs in a wish sent to someone starting something — a business, a course, a new job — and reads as fussy otherwise.

faqs.question: My Tamil message shows up as boxes or broken letters. What went wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually the text is not Unicode. Tamil uses a visible puḷḷi (U+0BCD) and only two conjunct ligatures, க்ஷ and ஶ்ரீ, so genuine Unicode Tamil renders on any current phone; boxes normally mean the text was copied from a site that still uses a pre-Unicode Tamil font encoding.

faqs.question: Can I send the same Tamil wish to a Sri Lankan or Malaysian Tamil friend?
faqs.answer: Yes — the words are identical. Richard Ishida's orthography notes record that the 1978 Tamil Nadu script reforms spread only within India and the digital world, while Sri Lanka, Singapore, Malaysia, Mauritius and Réunion kept the traditional syllable forms, so a few letters may simply look older to them.

faqs.question: Do I need a Tamil keyboard, or can I copy and paste the wish?
faqs.answer: Copy and paste works. Everything above is Unicode Tamil, so it survives a paste into WhatsApp, Instagram or a browser field without a Tamil keyboard installed.

faqs.question: What do I write to a Tamil colleague who does not celebrate the festival?
faqs.answer: Send wish 1 in English letters with the meaning attached, or skip the deity entirely and wish them a good long weekend. A benediction addressed to Pillaiyar is not a neutral message, and vazhthu means blessing rather than 'best wishes'.

faqs.question: Is it lazy to forward an image instead of typing the wish out?
faqs.answer: It reads that way to most people, and it costs you something practical: the Tamil in a JPEG cannot be copied, searched or read aloud by a screen reader. Live text also lets the recipient reply in Tamil without retyping your line.

faqs.question: How early should the wish go out?
faqs.answer: On the morning of 14 September, before the Madhyahna window opens at 10:51 AM in Chennai. Wishes sent the night before read as pre-scheduled, which is exactly the impression a hand-written Tamil line is meant to avoid.

faqs.question: I do not read Tamil script. Can I still send one of these?
faqs.answer: Yes. Send the Tamil line with the Roman transliteration underneath it, which is how second-generation and non-Tamil-reading senders normally do it, and keep the English meaning for yourself so you know what you are actually saying.

faqs.question: Does the person receiving a SubhSandesh page need to install anything?
faqs.answer: No. It opens as a web page in whatever browser is already on their phone, which matters because 49.6% of all 45,656 views SubhSandesh has recorded are on a phone — measured platform-wide across 15 page types, not on Ganesh pages.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ganesh Chaturthi Wishes in Tamil, Sent as Vinayagar Chaturthi

Ganesh Chaturthi wishes in Tamil are usually not written as "Ganesh Chaturthi" at all. In Tamil the day is விநாயகர் சதுர்த்தி (Vinayagar Chaturthi) or பிள்ளையார் சதுர்த்தி (Pillaiyar Chaturthi), and the greeting word is வாழ்த்துக்கள் (vazhthukkal), so the standard line reads இனிய விநாயகர் சதுர்த்தி நல்வாழ்த்துக்கள்.

The date is Monday 14 September 2026. [Drik Panchang's Chennai listing](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/ganesh-chaturthi/ganesh-chaturthi-date-time.html?geoname-id=1264527&year=2026) puts the Madhyahna puja muhurat at 10:51 AM to 1:18 PM, and Ganesha visarjan on Friday 25 September.

Send it as live text, not a forwarded JPEG. Across all 45,656 views of the 3,860 pages SubhSandesh has created since March 2026 — platform-wide across 15 page types, with no Ganesh-specific number behind it — 49.6% are opened on a phone, and 96.1% of started pages get published and shared.

Nine wishes follow in Tamil script, each with a transliteration and an English meaning, plus the three choices behind them: the name, the word for "obstacle", and literary Tamil or spoken.

## Vinayagar Chaturthi, Pillaiyar Chaturthi, and what vazhthukkal means

Tamil has three names for the day and they are not interchangeable. The University of Madras *Tamil Lexicon* carries **பிள்ளையார்சதுர்த்தி** as its own headword — "a festival in honour of Gaṇēša" — cross-referred to **விநாயகசதுர்த்தி**, with a third form, **பிள்ளையார்சவுதி**, marked as local.

பிள்ளையார் *piḷḷaiyār* is glossed first as **மகன், "son"**, and only then as Ganesha. That is the warm, domestic name — the child of the house. விநாயகர் is the formal one, and கணேஷ் is what you write when you are writing Hindi or English in Tamil letters.

The greeting word matters as much as the name. [The *Tamil Lexicon* defines வாழ்த்து](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%B5%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%B4%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%A4%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%A4%E0%AF%81&searchhws=yes) as "benediction, felicitation", its third sense being "invocation or praise of the deity at the beginning of a religious or literary work".

So வாழ்த்துக்கள் is not a casual "wishes". It is a blessing pronounced over someone, and its dictionary sense is literally the thing said before beginning — which on Vinayagar Chaturthi is exactly right.

## Nine Vinayagar Chaturthi vazhthukkal in Tamil, with transliteration and meaning

Ordered from safest to most specific, with the Tamil, a transliteration you can read aloud, and what it says.

### 1. The plain one, safe for anybody

**இனிய விநாயகர் சதுர்த்தி நல்வாழ்த்துக்கள்!**
*Iniya Vinayagar Chaturthi nalvazhthukkal!*
"Sweet Vinayagar Chaturthi good wishes." The default, safe for a boss or a WhatsApp group.

### 2. The Pillaiyar version, for an older relative

**பிள்ளையார் சதுர்த்தி வாழ்த்துக்கள்! அவர் அருள் உங்கள் குடும்பத்திற்குத் துணையாக இருக்கட்டும்.**
*Pillaiyar Chaturthi vazhthukkal! Avar arul ungal kudumbaththirku thunaiyaaga irukkattum.*
"Pillaiyar Chaturthi greetings. May his grace stand by your family." Older households say Pillaiyar far more often than Vinayagar, and an elder hears the difference.

### 3. The obstacle line, in native Tamil

**இடையூறுகள் யாவும் அகலட்டும்; நீங்கள் நினைத்தது நிறைவேறட்டும்.**
*Idaiyoorugal yaavum agalattum; neengal ninaiththathu niraivaerattum.*
"May every obstacle move aside; may what you have in mind be fulfilled." இடையூறு is the native Tamil word for obstacle, not the Sanskrit-derived one, and the next section explains why that is a decision.

### 4. For a new start, using the Pillaiyar suzhi

**பிள்ளையார் சுழி போட்டு ஒரு புதிய தொடக்கம். உங்கள் புதிய முயற்சி வெற்றி பெறட்டும்!**
*Pillaiyar suzhi pottu oru puthiya thodakkam. Ungal puthiya muyarchi vetri perattum!*
"A new beginning opened with the Pillaiyar suzhi. May your new venture succeed." The suzhi is the 'உ' mark the lexicon defines as drawn for auspiciousness when you begin to write — send this to someone starting a business or a course.

### 5. The kozhukattai line

**கொழுக்கட்டையின் இனிப்பு போல உங்கள் வாழ்க்கை இனிக்கட்டும்!**
*Kozhukattaiyin inippu pola ungal vaazhkkai inikkattum!*
"May your life be sweet like the sweetness of the kozhukattai." Naming kozhukattai instead of modak is the clearest single signal that a wish was written for a Tamil reader.

### 6. For a whole family, using the arugampul

**அறுகம்புல் போல உங்கள் குடும்பம் என்றும் பசுமையாகத் தழைக்கட்டும்.**
*Arugampul pola ungal kudumbam endrum pasumaiyaaga thazhaikkattum.*
"Like arugampul, may your family stay green and flourish." அறுகு is *Cynodon dactylon*, the grass the lexicon records as "used in ceremonies" — the durva laid at Pillaiyar's feet.

### 7. For someone who has had a hard year

**இந்த வருடம் கடினமாக இருந்தது. விநாயகர் அருளால் இனிவரும் நாட்கள் இலகுவாக அமையட்டும்.**
*Indha varudam kadinamaaga irundhadhu. Vinayagar arulaal inivarum naatkal ilaguvaaga amaiyattum.*
"This year has been hard. By Vinayagar's grace, may the days ahead come easier." Naming the bad year first is what separates this from a forward. Do not soften it.

### 8. Asking for a blessing instead of giving one

**உங்கள் வாழ்த்தும் பிள்ளையாரின் அருளும் எங்களுக்குக் கிடைக்கட்டும். சதுர்த்தி வாழ்த்துக்கள்!**
*Ungal vazhthum Pillaiyarin arulum engalukku kidaikkattum. Chaturthi vazhthukkal!*
"May we receive both your blessing and Pillaiyar's grace. Chaturthi greetings." Sent to a grandparent or a teacher, this reverses the direction of the vazhthu, which is the polite form.

### 9. Spoken Tamil, for a friend

**விநாயகர் சதுர்த்தி வாழ்த்துக்கள்ங்க! கொழுக்கட்டை சாப்பிட வீட்டுக்கு வாங்க.**
*Vinayagar Chaturthi vazhthukkalnga! Kozhukattai saappida veettukku vaanga.*
"Chaturthi greetings! Come over and eat kozhukattai." The -ங்க clitic and வாங்க are koduntamil, the spoken form: nobody prints this on a card and everybody types it on WhatsApp.

## Idaiyuru or vikkinam: a hundred-year-old argument inside a two-line greeting

Tamil has two words for the obstacle Vinayagar removes, and picking one is not neutral. The lexicon glosses **இடையூறு** as "impediment, obstruction, hindrance" and then defines **விக்கினம்** as "n. *vighna*. Obstacle, impediment, hindrance; இடையூறு" — marking it, in the entry itself, as the Sanskrit import.

That distinction has a movement behind it. In Harold Schiffman's chapter on Tamil language policy, the purist tradition — the *tanit tamiḻ iyakkam* — is dated from [Maraimalai Adigal's 1915–16 vow to speak only pure Tamil](https://www.sas.upenn.edu/~haroldfs/sars238/tamil238.html), after Caldwell's 1856 grammar and the 1880 rediscovery of the classical texts.

விக்கினம் is not wrong, and older devotional Tamil is full of it. But இடையூறு reads as Tamil written by a Tamil speaker, and விக்கினம் reads as translated Sanskrit, so use இடையூறு if you have no view on the argument.

## Centamil, koduntamil, and what people actually type on a phone

Written Tamil and spoken Tamil are different languages in practice. Schiffman calls Tamil "severely diglossic": the literary variety shows few changes since its thirteenth-century codification by Pavanandi, spoken Tamil has changed radically over the same period, and despite rising literacy "diglossia shows no signs of diminishing".

Richard Ishida's [Tamil orthography notes](https://r12a.github.io/scripts/taml/ta.html), updated 28 April 2026, agree: the classic form is preferred for writing and public speaking, and the colloquial form differs widely from it. Wishes 1 to 8 are centamil; wish 9 is koduntamil, and sending it to a grandmother reads as sloppy rather than warm.

Script is the second decision. A corpus of 15,744 code-mixed Tamil sentences, filtered from 184,573 YouTube comments, reports that [most comments were written in Roman script](https://aclanthology.org/2020.sltu-1.28/) rather than Tamil script, because Tanglish needs no Tamil keyboard.

That describes a comment thread, not a greeting. Romanised Tamil is fine between friends; to an elder, English letters look like you could not be bothered to switch keyboards. Ishida also records that the 1978 Tamil Nadu script reforms spread only in India and the digital world, so a Sri Lankan or Malaysian reader may hold older syllable forms to be the correct ones.

## Kozhukattai is not modak, and the wish should say so

The Maharashtrian word is modak; the Tamil word is **கொழுக்கட்டை**, kozhukattai — defined in the *Tamil Lexicon* as a bolus of rice flour with coconut scrapings and jaggery. The telling part: its entry for **மோதகம்**, *modakam*, sends you back to கொழுக்கட்டை rather than the other way round.

So the Sanskrit-derived word exists in Tamil and is simply not the everyday one. "May your day be as sweet as the modak" is a Marathi wish wearing Tamil letters, and Tamil readers notice.

The same applies to the offering: arugampul, red hibiscus and kozhukattai are what actually reaches a Tamil Pillaiyar. SubhSandesh's [Ganesh Chaturthi page the recipient performs themselves](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) — they offer the durva and the flowers, circle the aarti thali, and write their own prarthana back — only earns its place if the Tamil on it is the Tamil they would use.

## What it costs to send a Vinayagar Chaturthi wish four ways

Four channels, compared on cost and on what survives the trip.

| Way to send it | Cost | Tamil stays live, selectable text | Locked to one recipient |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forwarded JPEG from a wishes site | ₹0 | No — the Tamil is pixels, uncopyable and unsearchable | No |
| Typed into WhatsApp yourself | ₹0 | Yes, if you have a Tamil keyboard installed | No |
| Printed Tamil card, couriered inside Tamil Nadu | ₹150–₹400, 2–4 days | No | No |
| A shareable SubhSandesh page | ₹0 to create | Yes, as Unicode in the browser | Yes — 42.1% of creators (1,625 of 3,860, platform-wide) set a password before sharing |

The password column is the one no competitor can fill. That 42.1% is measured across all 15 SubhSandesh page types, not Ganesh pages, but the point holds: people writing something personal often do not want it forwarded on. To see how Tamil script sits inside a page, [browse the other SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) or open the [animated shaadi card](https://subhsandesh.in/shaadi-card).

One more platform-wide number, sampled on 1,065 love-gf pages rather than Ganesh ones: the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.8 hours. People come back to fix wording, which is what you want in a script you type slowly.

## Where a Tamil wishes page loses

A page cannot hand anyone a kozhukattai, and it cannot stand you in front of the Pillaiyar at the end of your street on 14 September. If you are in the same city, go, and take the sweet with you.

It also loses with a recipient who has no smartphone — the platform-wide 49.6% mobile-open rate implies the other half of views are not on phones at all. A grandmother who reads Tamil on paper rather than glass is better served by a card in your handwriting, or a phone call in koduntamil.

And if you cannot check the Tamil, do not send Tamil. A wrong vowel sign lands worse than the same sentiment in clear English, because it reads as a machine-translated forward.

## Sources

- [*Tamil Lexicon*, University of Madras (1924–36), Digital Dictionaries of South Asia](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%B5%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%B4%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%A4%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%A4%E0%AF%81&searchhws=yes) — headwords வாழ்த்து, பிள்ளையார், கொழுக்கட்டை, மோதகம், இடையூறு, விக்கினம், அறுகு.
- Harold F. Schiffman, ["Language Policy and Linguistic Culture in Tamilnadu"](https://www.sas.upenn.edu/~haroldfs/sars238/tamil238.html), chapter 6 of *Linguistic Culture and Language Policy* — diglossia and the *tanit tamiḻ iyakkam*.
- Chakravarthi, Muralidaran, Priyadharshini and McCrae, ["Corpus Creation for Sentiment Analysis in Code-Mixed Tamil-English Text"](https://aclanthology.org/2020.sltu-1.28/), SLTU–CCURL, LREC, May 2020.
- Richard Ishida, ["Tamil orthography notes"](https://r12a.github.io/scripts/taml/ta.html), updated 28 April 2026.
- [Drik Panchang, Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 for Chennai](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/ganesh-chaturthi/ganesh-chaturthi-date-time.html?geoname-id=1264527&year=2026) — date and Madhyahna muhurat.

auditReport.honestAssessment: The five pages in this SERP are regional wishes farms and a Pinterest pin: none prints a Roman transliteration, none gives an English meaning, none has a table or an FAQ, and the top news result is still stamped 2025. This post has four things they cannot copy without doing the work — the Tamil Lexicon's own cross-reference from மோதகம் to கொழுக்கட்டை, its marking of விக்கினம் as the Sanskrit loan for இடையூறு, the fact that கணேஷ் needs a Grantha letter that விநாயகர் and பிள்ளையார் do not, and the Chennai Madhyahna muhurat. Against that, subhsandesh.in has no Tamil-language authority and no Ganesh authority at all, the /happy-ganesh-chaturthi template it links has produced zero pages and currently 404s, and every first-party number here is platform-wide rather than segment-specific — so this is a citation play for answer engines, not a rank prediction. The real risk is linguistic, not technical: the nine wishes were composed and checked headword-by-headword against the Tamil Lexicon, but no native Tamil reader has reviewed them, and one clumsy line loses this audience faster than any ranking factor. Note for the batch: this post takes aclanthology.org to 3 of 3, so no wave-3 sibling may add an ACL source.
